mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a slowdown in economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a month, it signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST declines and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase by more than 1% in a quarter, it signals a strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and RSAFS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
